note: Re-judged 2026-11-02 by an independent auditor who authored none of the bgp-role changes. RFC 9234 Section 4.2: "When operating in the "strict mode", if the BGP Role Capability is sent but one is not received, the connection is rejected using the Role Mismatch Notification (code 2, subcode 11)." The only change to the file-scoped .ci units it judged (655d07b59b, 3459b6e390) deletes the `policy { reject-asn NO-TRANSIT { indirect [ 3356 ] } }` block, its four comment lines, and `filters [ inactive:NO-TRANSIT ];` from each bound import and export chain, leaving `final accept;`. That filter was deactivated and never ran; it existed only because the config then required a role's bound chain to name a transit-refusing filter, and 655d07b59b made that check a filter the bgp-role plugin inserts itself. Every OPEN capability option, every action=send and every expect/reject line (the exact NOTIFICATION or UPDATE hex) is byte-identical, so each case still isolates the same condition and asserts the same exact outcome. The discrimination records on these .ci carriers (validateOpenRolePair) were re-taken over the changed units in this session. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgement follows. Rejudged 2026-10-31 by an auditor who authored none of the change. The only change to test/plugin/role-strict-enforcement.ci since the last stamp is cabb706c11 moving the policy block from inside bgp {} to the top-level policy root, the same lines re-indented; every action, expect, reject and option line is byte-identical, so the carriers drive the same inputs and assert the same outcomes. Verdict unchanged. RFC 9234 Section 4.2: "An operator may choose to apply a "strict mode" in which the receipt of a BGP Role Capability from the remote AS is required." "When operating in the "strict mode", if the BGP Role Capability is sent but one is not received, the connection is rejected using the Role Mismatch Notification (code 2, subcode 11)." role/validate.go::validateOpenRolePair branches on cfg.strict when peerRoles is empty. role-strict-enforcement.ci configures customer and strict true, drops capability 9 from the remote OPEN and requires exact NOTIFICATION 2/11. TestValidateOpenStrictModeRefusesADynamicGroupMemberWithNoRole checks strict refusal with 2/11 and acceptance of the corresponding group member; TestValidateOpenRolePair_NoPeerRole_NoStrict accepts a missing remote role with strict false. The adjacent backward-compatibility sentence says SHOULD ignore absence, not MUST; the negative pins the chosen non-strict behavior without upgrading that SHOULD. The functional fixture remains ASN 1/1 as before; it is supplemented by the role/group unit controls, not described as an eBGP wire fixture. Rejudged independently against RFC source and every tagged carrier on 2026-10-22. Functional judgments use the corresponding test/draft/plugin files, not the unpromoted old-syntax live files. Their inactive NO-TRANSIT import/export policies explicitly end in accept; reactor runEgressPolicyChain applies that final only after mandatory in-process OTC, and OPEN validation is independent. This is a source judgment, not a new runtime or discrimination result; parent owns promotion and native freshness before stamping.
